newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's outlawed labour union votes to strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's outlawed labour union votes to strike.

text.p: Members of South Korea's outlawed labour union on Wednesday voted overwhelmingly to strike in protest against the government's labour reform plans, a union spokesman said.
Chung Sung-hee, a spokesman for the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, said 251,764 members at about 300 companies voted on a proposal to strike this month.
Around 90 percent voted in favour of industrial action, although the exact result would not be known until Thursday, he said. The timing of the strike would be decided by union leaders on Friday.
On Tuesday the government unveiled a plan to revise labour legislation. The union objects to articles that open the way to worker layoffs and flexible working hours.
